question: Compare semaglutide 1 mg and empagliflozin 25 mg over 30 weeks

reply.text:
Interpreted as: semaglutide 1 mg, empagliflozin 25 mg; 30 weeks; 200 per arm. Simulated 30-week trial with 200 patients per arm. Semaglutide 1 mg/week: HbA1c -1.644 points against placebo (95% interval -1.824 to -1.464), weight -4.061 kg; Empagliflozin 25 mg/day: HbA1c -0.815 points against placebo (95% interval -1.073 to -0.634), weight -2.408 kg. Validation on 20 held-out real results: mean HbA1c error 0.29 points. Accuracy check FAILED, interval coverage passed, kidney check passed, and it did not beat a simple rival with no physiology. Kidney behaviour was tested only for empagliflozin at eGFR 30 to 90. Blind test record for semaglutide: Semaglutide phase 2 (12 weeks, 6 results) over-predicted the HbA1c benefit by 0.50 on average: missed; SUSTAIN 2 (56 weeks, 2 results) over-predicted the HbA1c benefit by 0.09 on average: held up. Blind test record for empagliflozin: EMPA-REG MET (24 weeks, 2 results) over-predicted the HbA1c benefit by 0.17 on average: held up; EMPA-REG RENAL (24 weeks, 3 results) under-predicted the HbA1c benefit by 0.02 on average: held up. Hypoglycaemia is not modelled. Risk rises with sulfonylureas or insulin. Research simulation. Not medical advice and not evidence that a treatment works in any person.

question: What side effects were reported for semaglutide?

reply.text:
Semaglutide, from its FDA label: Thyroid c-cell tumors (boxed warning): Thyroid C-cell tumors occurred in rodents. It is unknown whether this happens in humans. Pancreatitis (warning): Acute pancreatitis has been observed with GLP-1 receptor agonists. Retinopathy (warning): Diabetic retinopathy complications have been reported. Hypoglycemia (warning): Risk of low blood sugar rises when used with insulin or an insulin secretagogue. Most common events in real trial NCT02054897 (not simulated): Nausea 20.3%, Diarrhoea 12.5%, Headache 11.7%, Constipation 6.2%, Lipase increased 6.2%. Label warnings come first because this table cannot show them: one trial, at the reporting threshold the sponsor chose, is too small for rare but serious harms. An event missing from the table means it was not reported at that threshold, and does not mean it cannot happen. These rates are not simulated. For any concern about a medicine, please ask a doctor or pharmacist.
